title: Senolytics: The latest trend in anti-aging research explained
abstract:
### Difference to other anti-ageing substances  
In contrast to conventional anti-ageing substances, which often only treat the symptoms of ageing, senolytics tackle the causes directly. While many anti-ageing products only bring about superficial improvements, senolytics eliminate the senescent cells and thus fundamentally improve cell regeneration. Examples such as quercetin and dasatinib have shown in studies not only an improvement in kidney function and a reduction in the risk of kidney failure, but also a significant increase in physical activity in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis by reducing cell ageing.
### Results and findings from animal experiments  
Animal studies have shown that senolytics such as dasatinib and quercetin have significant effects on the lifespan and healthspan of laboratory animals. In studies on mice, the administration of senolytics extended life expectancy by almost 10%. This confirms the potential of these substances to reduce the effect of senescent cells and thus promote general health.  
Another important result of the animal studies is the improvement of specific organ functions. In a mouse study, fisetin was found to improve kidney function and reduce fibrosis. Quercetin has shown similar positive effects in kidney studies, underlining the role of senolytics in the regeneration and maintenance of healthy organs.
### Synthetic senolytics: Dasatinib  
Dasatinib, a drug originally developed for the treatment of leukemia, has also recently gained importance as a senolytic substance. In combination with quercetin, dasatinib has shown impressive results in research studies. This combination has the potential to effectively eliminate senescent cells in the body and promote general well-being.  
Dasatinib acts directly on certain signaling pathways that are activated in senescent cells, thereby contributing to the promotion of new, healthy cells. This offers a promising perspective for future therapeutic applications, particularly in the treatment and prevention of age-related diseases.
